the_ruling_verbatim: any anything can be expressly delegated. at the moment i cannot think of anything that should be implicitly delegated, but that's not a comprehensive search.
given that i can think of no reason to limit delegation. each device is a delegate for a specific set of capabilities.
now_the_spec_says: Delegation is flat and unlimited when explicit — any admitted hand may mint for any other. No implicit delegation case is known. Crypto signing is deferred to the multi-trust-domain boundary (a second box or a second user); on a single box the filesystem IS the identity and signing would be security theater.
what_dies: The open question on artifact d830a3f80723 (bullet 3): whether mint_grant should allow nested/restricted delegation. Answer: no restriction needed.
The still_open question on ticket 0354c0269ff7 (an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands): who may MINT on an intention's behalf. Answer: any admitted hand.

resolves_ticket_question.disposition: The flat mint_grant model is correct as built. The nested-capability question is answered: no nesting needed.
